newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasuries end lower as 10-year sale awaited.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasuries end lower as 10-year sale awaited.

text.p: The prices of U.S. Treasury securities closed slightly lower on Tuesday as the Treasury's 10-year note sale was awaited.
The Treasury's three-year auction produced average yields of 6.041 percent, slightly higher than anticipated.

Aside from the Treasury's auction of three-year notes, there were few important data releases for the market. Leading economic indicators came in unchanged for June and U.S. housing completions fell 7.8 percent in June. The Redbook report showed sales up 0.3 percent in the most recent period.
"The market is vulnerable here (at current price levels)," said Anthony Karadakis, senior financial economist at First National Bank of Chicago. "The key test will be the 10-year auction tomorrow."
Karadakis said that if the dealer community managed to take down the 10-year paper and improve in price tone, the worst of its worries would be behind it.
"There's a tug of war between the bulls and bears right now. There's more a better balance than there has been for months," he said. But the market was clearly in a dispirited mood, he added.

"It would be hard to imagine we're going to make much progress before the auctions are over. Until these are finished, there will be increased worry about the economy and federal monetary policy," said Hugh Johnson, chief economist at First Albany Corp.
"A week ago, few would have wagered that the Federal Reserve would move in August, or even September," Johnson said. That has now changed, he said.
He said there was a sense of tentativeness in the market currently, but most of the short-term losses already may have been incurred following Friday's selloff.
The Treasury's quarterly refunding operation continues on Wednesday with the sale of $12 billion of 10-year issues and $10 billion of 30-year bonds on Thursday.
The signing of a balanced budget deal in Washington had little market impact as dealers already had priced the accord into market prices.
San Francisco Fed president Robert Parry spoke on Tuesday, saying the Fed was prepared to head off inflationary pressures, but his comments got little notice with two auctions still on tap.
The Treasury's 30-year bond was closing 6/32 lower at 101-23/32 to yield 6.49 percent.
The 10-year issue was at 102-26/32, off 3/32 to yield 6.24 percent. The five-year issue was down 2/32 at 99-15/32 to yield 6.13 percent. The two-year was 1/32 lower at 99-29/32 to yield 5.93 percent.

At the short end of the maturity spectrum, the three-month bill rate was one basis point higher at 5.15 percent and the six-month and year bills rates were each up two basis points at 5.21 percent and 5.24 percent, respectively.
